what_this_is: Measured effects of serving this checkpoint at 1,000,000 tokens via Qwen's official static YaRN recipe on the 8x DP8 host: KV capacity, needle retrieval up to 99.5 % of the window, and a prefill cost law fitted across four window sizes.

config.method: official Qwen static YaRN, factor 4.0, original_max_position_embeddings 262144

kv_capacity.derivation: only 16 of 64 layers carry KV (48 are linear-attention GDN with O(1) state); at fp8 that is 2 x 4 kv-heads x 256 head_dim x 1 B x 16 layers = 32768 B = 32 KiB per token
kv_capacity.cross_check: 1,879,687 x 32 KiB = 61.6 GiB against the engine's reported 62.45 GiB
kv_capacity.independent_corroboration: the vLLM recipe page states 6.6M KV tokens at 1M context on a 288 GB GB300; 6.6M x 32 KiB = 206 GiB, which fits that card and confirms 32 KiB/token from an outside source
kv_capacity.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT: paged KV allocates per token USED, not per max-model-len. Setting --max-model-len 1000000 reserves nothing. Real agent traffic at 10-100k tokens is unaffected by these full-length figures; the 1.88-per-GPU number only binds for sequences that actually fill the window.
kv_capacity.effect_of_raising_the_window_on_pool_siz: essentially none - the 262k config measured 1,776,428 KV tokens and the 1M config measures 1,879,687. The pool is whatever remains after weights and activations, so the window setting does not shrink it.

needle_retrieval.verdict: retrieval PASS at every rung, up to 99.5 % of a 1M window
needle_retrieval.gate_verdict_note: the 1M gate's OVERALL verdict was FAIL, but not for retrieval: check 3 timed out on one probe under production load, and check 3 was separately found vacuous (receipts/gate-check3-vacuous.json). needle_retrieval itself PASSED at 994,755 tokens.

prefill_cost_law.headline: k rises monotonically and CROSSES 2 at the top of the window
prefill_cost_law.mechanism: this is a hybrid model: 48 of 64 layers are linear attention, cost O(n), and 16 of 64 are full attention, cost O(n^2). At short n the linear majority dominates and k sits near 1.5; by 1M the quadratic minority owns the cost and k passes 2. The rising exponent IS the architecture becoming visible.

registered_prediction.basis: k=1.584 fitted on the first three rungs only
registered_prediction.lesson: the prediction under-shot because k is not constant; a single global exponent under-predicts the tail

prefill_cost_law.practical_consequence: a 1M-token prompt costs 2.53x MORE PER TOKEN to prefill than a 262k prompt. Long context is not linearly priced on this architecture, and any per-token cost model that ignores window size will understate long-context traffic by up to 2.5x.

honest_limits: Every wall-clock number here was measured while a TB2.1 arm ran at C16 on the same endpoint, so absolute tok/s are depressed by contention.
The longer rungs span more wall clock and therefore more varied contention, so the exponent carries that noise; the MONOTONE RISE is robust but the exact k values are not to three digits.
One needle position (mid-document, char-depth 0.5) and one document generator; this is retrieval, not long-context reasoning.
Static YaRN is applied at all lengths, so short-context behaviour under this config is a separate question (measured elsewhere).
